title: Rivalry Week Is Here To Ruin Some Postseason Plans
summary: Welcome to the Defector College Football Watch Guide , where Israel Daramola and Ray Ratto will tell you which of the weekend’s college football games are worth giving a crap about. Ray: It's seeds-and-stems time in the college football season, and if that only means something for you older stoners, a glimpse at the schedule should tell you just how desirable that is. It's Rivalry Week for those schools that have a natural rival, and plain old Week The Last for everyone else. But even the rivalry games don't burn the way they used to. Indiana is now light years ahead of Purdue, Michigan vs. Ohio State feels unusually trivial and bleak this season, and South Carolina-Clemson is just a meaningless referendum on Dabo Swinney you didn't need or ask for. In other news, the NCAA is running a test on the 24-team playoff on Sunday with the announcement of the FCS playoff bracket, which is to say the Dakotas/Montanas Range War. The FCS champion in 12 of the past 15 years has been absorbed by those FBS ghouls, and since most of those champions have been North Dakota State (now an FBS operation; they won 10 of those titles ), South Dakota State, and most recently Montana State, it seems safe to say the FCS trophy route runs roughly in parallel to I-90. But that's tomorrow's apocalypse. Saturday's opening round includes Harvard at Monmouth at noon ET, Idaho State at North Dakota at 1 p.m., and Incarnate Word at Montana at 8 p.m. The first two are on ESPN+, and UIW-Montana is on ESPNU, which is good news for you small-school psychos.
